scope: The opt-in createCoreKeyTupleEngine routes encode through the retained Rust runtime using a one-shot prefix stage: source, identity, and values are admitted separately, Rust checks identity and the current source version, and only then does the host admit options and complete encoding.

Source, identity, values, options, receipt, and current each retain the predecessor per-argument 100,000-value ceiling; a crossed-argument control proves the direct route does not impose a narrower aggregate ceiling.

The staged encode carries one host-control bridge and Rust TransportUsage across prefix admission and options/final encode. Verify and raw-byte reads use a fresh one-shot receipt-first prepareVerification stage with the same cumulative control/usage behavior.
PreparedCoreKeyTuples still returns the predecessor-shaped frozen object with exactly profile, source, encode, and verify.
Public createCoreModelEngine remains eager and tuple-capable; createCoreModelRootEngine continues to omit tuple methods; no default export route changed.
